label: JZ Mock B · Paper 2 · Question 3
knowledgePattern: Find a smallest lucky set of truth checks that singles out an option
solution:
For a single check of statements 1, 2, 3, 4, the numbers of options with a true response are respectively 3, 4, 3, 2. The corresponding false-response counts are 6, 5, 6, 7. None is one, so one check can never determine the option.

If checks of statements 1 and 3 both return true, only option F in the inner list is compatible. Therefore two checks can be enough in a lucky case, and fewer cannot. The required number is 2: answer B in the outer answer list.

hints.title: Cross out options after one check
hints.body: Choose one statement to check. First suppose it is true and cross out every incompatible option; then try the same check with a false reply.
hints.recap: You know the answer only when one listed option remains.
hints.pitfall: Use the full inner list A–I, not the final answer choices.
hints.pause: See whether any single check and reply leaves just one option.

recall.reminder: Check all the listed cases before ruling out a possibility.

hints.title: Look for a lucky set of replies
hints.body: Try another statement on the options that remain. You only need one possible run of replies that identifies the answer.
hints.recap: Prove both that your number of checks can work and that fewer cannot.
hints.pitfall: The question asks for the lucky minimum, not the worst case.
hints.pause: Find a successful sequence of checks and justify why it is shortest.

recall.reminder: A smallest value needs a reason smaller values fail and an example that works.
